Beautiful, the herring was cut by a lefthanded person, probably the painter himself. Fuck me I'm hungry now.

The knife may have (and really probably) been placed there for compositional reasons. If I view the piece as a narrative then it was a left handed person. When I look at it as an artist I just see the compositional elements.

The knife on the left on a diagonal creates a strong triangle which helps keep the eye within the picture. If we place it on the right it will either create an angle which leads down and out which we don't want. We could also place it on the right and at a vertical, but that makes for a more boring composition and it places too much weight on the right hand side making an unbalanced composition. All of this is also why the beer and the roll have been placed as they are.

Composing the elements w/in a piece are the early choices which make a piece strong.

It's not only the knife. Also the position of the herring, you fillet it from head to tail, so either the plate was turned around, or it was filleted by a southpaw.

I understand that this tableau was composed for artistic merrit as when I would have set it for myself, the herring would be on the bread and the beer would be already half empty.

Anyway I was quickly jumping to conclusions as I had lunch to make.
